# decimal128 text codec -- parse-direction test vectors.
# TextCodecLayer.md Section 8.2 (Phase 1). Generated 2026-08-22.
#
# COLUMNS  input_text , expected_bid_hex , expected_dpd_hex , status
#
# input_text is ALWAYS double-quoted, with \\ and \" escapes. The three files in
# this directory that predate these leave their text column bare, which they can
# afford because every row there is round-trippable canonical output. These
# tables are input-driven, so the text column has to carry the empty string, a
# leading or trailing space, and an embedded comma -- none of which survive a
# bare comma-separated field. (resources/rosetta/native/parse.txt hit the same
# wall and punted: its header lists the empty string, "1 " and "nan 1" as cases
# its space-delimited grammar could not carry.)
#
# The hex columns are 0x + 32 UPPERCASE hex digits, most-significant word first,
# matching the sibling files. status is the SCREAMING_SNAKE token (D6).
#
# PROVENANCE. Expected values come from decimal128-c -- the FULL port -- via its
# public d128_parse / d128_to_bid128 / d128_to_dpd128. That engine uses the
# reciprocal-multiply divPow10 and the five-mode Round table; the codecs use the
# D3 table-free kernel and a ties-to-even specialization. So the oracle is
# genuinely independent of what these vectors test. Every row was then run
# through decimal128-text-codec-c and matched bit-for-bit, and the accept/reject
# decision was confirmed identical between the two engines on all 1078 inputs.
#
# ROUNDING IS TIES-TO-EVEN THROUGHOUT. Per D2 the codec takes no rounding
# direction, so these vectors carry no rounding-mode column. The dectest-derived
# rows are drawn ONLY from blocks under `rounding: half_even`; dqBase's other six
# directives are inapplicable and reduce out.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# T4 ERROR -- malformed input -> status token.
#
# The bid/dpd columns are NOT padding. Section 4 requires that parse ALWAYS
# writes its out-parameter, so that a caller who discards the status still
# observes a legal IEEE 754-2019 datum rather than stale memory. Every row here
# carries the canonical positive quiet NaN those columns must contain, so a port
# can assert the written value and not merely the status.
#
# Sources: dqBase.decTest's own conversion-syntax cases (which trace to Rosetta),
# the failure rows of resources/rosetta/native/parse.txt, and the digit-separator
# cases from Section 6.4 -- including the five "followed by a digit" vectors that
# every port in the family wrongly accepted until 2026-08-22.
#
# NOTE on "_1": a LEADING underscore never reaches the coefficient loop, because
# the top-level dispatch tests the first character and '_' is neither a digit, a
# dot, nor the start of a non-finite word. It lands on INVALID_FORMAT, not
# INVALID_UNDERSCORE_LOCATION. That is decimal128-c's behavior and every port
# inherits it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
